AI in Banking & Financial Services.
The middle office is the last analog mile.

Watch the film, then read why governed agents — not more copilots — close it.

THE POV · 40 SECONDS
01 — Where the industry stands

Credit where due.

Banks in the region have digitized the customer with real distinction: onboarding in minutes, world-class apps, instant payments, open-banking rails. Fraud models run in production and digital channels carry the majority of interactions. This is not an industry that fears technology — it is an industry that has repeatedly absorbed it and grown.

02 — The pitfalls we keep seeing

Not failures of ambition. Patterns.

1

The middle office never got the memo

credit files, leasing applications, KYC refresh and reconciliation still run on analysts re-keying documents between systems.

2

Copilot sprawl

assistants that advise but never execute lift individual productivity a little and process outcomes not at all.

3

Model risk fear freezes deployment

without auditability by architecture, every AI initiative queues behind compliance indefinitely.

4

Point-solution procurement

ten vendors, ten pilots, no operating model.

POV
03 — Our point of view

Challenging the status quo.

The status quo says AI in banking means chat assistants and fraud scores. We disagree. The value in a bank sits in document-heavy, rule-bound decision flows — credit, leasing, trade, disputes — and those yield only to governed agents that prepare complete, cited decision files while accountable bankers decide. Regulator-explainable is not a constraint on this design; it is the design.

04 — Three levels of value

Each level funds the next.

L1 — Individual assistantsAI assistants for every banker: drafting, summarizing statements and files, first-pass analysis
+35%
8 weeks
L2 — Agentic functionsCredit decisioning, leasing ops, RM desk, contact center run as governed agentic processes
+65%
3–6 months
L3 — Agentic enterpriseSelected domains operate autonomously under human gates, continuously optimized
+95%
6–12 months

The ambition: Thousands of FTEs of capacity created without hiring — and a bank whose middle office moves as fast as its app.

05 — Where to start

Concrete plays, not concepts.

01
Core credit & leasing operations

clean-file credit decisions in under an hour, down from 2–3 analyst-days; every gate auditable and explainable to the regulator by design.

02
Contact center sales & service

human-sounding voice AI, fully on-premise so voice and data never leave the bank; inbound and outbound, executing actions, not just answering.

03
Statement intelligence

bank and card statements itemized and merchant-normalized for underwriting, reconciliation and disputes (CogniDocs).

04
AI-SDLC

the bank's own engineers amplified: about 50% reduction in delivery lead time, starting where output can be mechanically verified.

06 — Prove it in 60 days

48 hours to a prototype.
Day 60: the evidence.

No belief required — a working prototype, a live MVP, and the data to decide where to scale.

AI in Public Sector & Government.
One operating system beats a hundred pilots.

Why the gap in government AI is architectural — and how ministries close it.

THE POV · 40 SECONDS
01 — Where the industry stands

Credit where due.

Gulf governments run some of the most advanced digital services in the world — unified portals, digital identity, services measured in minutes. Whole-of-government platforms exist here that mature democracies still debate. The ambition gap is zero.

02 — The pitfalls we keep seeing

Not failures of ambition. Patterns.

1

AI arrives as point solutions

a chatbot here, an OCR tool there — and most stall in exploratory pilots that never scale (the pattern OECD documents across members).

2

The same service patterns

apply, get a decision, pay — are rebuilt per service, per department.

3

Institutional knowledge is retiring faster than it is being captured.

4

Oversight is guidance-only: few formal standards, fewer algorithm registers

so trust cannot compound.

POV
03 — Our point of view

Challenging the status quo.

The status quo says buy more tools. We say entities need an operating system: one conversational front door, an orchestrated agent workforce grounded in the entity's own laws, governed human-in-the-loop workflows, institutional memory, and explicit AI governance. When we mapped one ministry's operations, 87% of thousands of steps followed patterns covered by 14 reusable blocks. Governments don't need a hundred pilots; they need those blocks, composed well, under governance — sovereign and Arabic-first by design.

Each level funds the next.

+95%
6–12 months

The ambition: A government that sees itself in real time — every process governed, every decision attributed, every bottleneck visible.

one registry, chat-first, bilingual; first domains live end to end with full audit.

03
Investor & citizen journeys

agentic front and back office: soft-landing of companies cut from 4 days to 4 minutes.

04
Institutional memory

the retiring generation's knowledge captured as a governed, queryable asset.

03 — Our point of view

Challenging the status quo.

For a group, the prize isn't a smarter factory — it's decision velocity across the holding. One agentic layer over the ERP estate gives the center a live view and gives every operating company shared digital workers instead of duplicated pilots. The group that runs procurement, finance ops and planning with a common agent workforce compounds an advantage no single subsidiary can buy.

Act I — This morning, somewhere in your organization

Aisha needs five days of leave. Watch what happens to her request.

It travels by email, waits in an inbox, gets tracked in someone's spreadsheet — and ends with a person re-typing the decision into a letter.

Every step works. Every person is competent. But the process lives in people's heads, the record lives in fragments, and leadership sees none of it until next month's report. Multiply Aisha by every request, in every department, every day.

Act II — What we found when we mapped the work

We mapped thousands of process steps and analyzed them. The work was trying to tell us something.

Organizations don't need hundreds of AI pilots. They need one operating system — a small set of blocks, composed well, under governance. That's why most AI arrives as point solutions… and stalls.

CogniOS. An operating system, not another app.

Like any OS, it doesn't replace what you run — it connects it. CogniOS sits on top of your existing systems and gives the whole organization one way to ask, one way to decide, and one memory. Arabic and English as equals, on every screen.

INTRODUCING COGNIDOCS

The documents machines could never read.

CogniDocs reads the world's hardest documents — architectural, mechanical, electrical and oil-installation drawings, bank and card statements — and turns them into itemized, classified, auditable data at 90%+ accuracy.

Read. Itemize. Classify. Prove it.

Book a demo See how ↓
COGNIDOCS · BANK STATEMENT
Act I — The blind spot

The world's money and infrastructure run on documents that were never written for machines.

Drawings are drawn, not written

A floor plan's most important facts aren't text — they're lines, symbols and dimensions. Labels get drawn as outlines. Scale bars lie. OCR sees pixels; the meaning lives in the geometry.

Statements speak in cipher

Every bank, a different format. Every line, a cryptic string — “CRM*CAREEM RIDES DXB 8842” means nothing to a ledger. Multiply by thousands of templates that change without notice.

So people re-type

Armies of analysts and engineers transcribing, reconciling, and re-checking — slow, expensive, and exactly where errors hide. The data was always there; nobody could read it.

Act II — The breakthrough

One reading engine. Three layers deep.

No single technique can read these documents — so CogniDocs doesn't use one. Three extraction layers read every document independently, then fuse: what one layer misses, another catches. That fusion is the IP — and it's what pushes accuracy past 90% at production speed.

And it refuses to guess. AI finds things; deterministic code does every measurement, comparison and sum. Where the evidence is insufficient, CogniDocs says so — every extracted item carries its source and its confidence.

Fused together: 90%+ accuracy — with every item traceable to exactly where it was found.

One engine, two editions

Wherever documents hold the numbers, CogniDocs gets them out.

COGNIDOCS FINANCE

Statements become structured, categorized data.

Bank and card statements from any institution, itemized line by line — with merchant names normalized against a global database of hundreds of thousands of brands and categorized by industry.

  • Merchant intelligence — “AMZN MKTP US*2K4” resolves to Amazon, e-commerce. An AI matcher finds the right brand even in mangled descriptors.
  • Self-learning formats — the first statement of a new format teaches the engine; every one after processes in seconds.
  • Every line auditable — amount, date, merchant, category, and the exact spot on the page it came from.
ReconciliationLending & underwritingExpense management Accounting data entrySpend analyticsAudit tie-outsFraud & tampering checksVAT recoveryDispute resolutionWealth & mortgage onboarding
COGNIDOCS ENGINEERING

Drawings become itemized, checkable bills of fact.

Every discipline of a drawing pack — architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, energy efficiency — plus pipeline and oil-installation drawings and BIM models. Read natively (DWG · DXF · vector PDF · IFC), itemized at a 90%+ hit rate, and pinned to sheet and location.

  • The whole pack, all disciplines — a real submission spans architectural, structural, mechanical and electrical sheets; CogniDocs reads them all in one pass.
  • Native CAD reading — dimensions and layers read straight out of the file as data, not guessed from an image. Each sheet derives its own scale.
  • Evidence-pinned findings — every quantity and verdict points to the exact sheet and spot a reviewer should look.
  • On-premise ready — runs offline on ordinary hardware; drawings never have to leave the building.

The problem

Integration is where agent projects go to die.

The demo–production gap

The agent that dazzled in the sandbox meets the real ERP — and stalls for months in brittle glue code, auth mazes and change-request queues.

LLMs deciding money

A probabilistic model approving credit or posting journals is a regulator's nightmare. Extraction is AI's job; decisions with legal or financial effect need rules that always answer the same way.

Every project, new plumbing

Each agent build re-solves connectors, retries, idempotency and audit — the same undifferentiated plumbing, paid for again and again.

FABRIC
